A 90-second instrumental track: the record playing on a speaker in the living room at a small, friendly evening gathering of friends at home. A warm, mellow neo-soul / lounge-jazz trio, recorded clean and close: a Fender Rhodes electric piano with soft amp tremolo carrying the chords (soft, round attacks), a round, warm fingered electric bass on roots and fifths, and a very soft kit played with brushes on the snare and a soft felt kick on the first beat of each bar. Slow 6/8 lilt: dotted quarter = 70 bpm, two swaying beats per bar, each divided in three; one bar lasts about 1.7 seconds. In tune at A = 440. Key: D minor (Dorian). A four-bar loop, one chord per bar, repeating throughout: Dm9 | G13 | Cmaj9 | A7(b9); the Rhodes top voice falls E, E, D, B-flat across the four bars. No lead instrument apart from an occasional short, lazy Rhodes fill. Relaxed, comfortable and unflashy.
[0:00 - 0:20] Already playing from the very first downbeat, sparse: Rhodes chords and bass only, quiet and relaxed.
[0:20 - 0:34] Soft brushes come in on the same loop.
[0:34 - 1:01] Fuller: the felt kick and brushes steady, the bass a little busier, a short Rhodes fill every four bars.
[1:01 - 1:30] Fullest, but still laid-back, with a little more Rhodes movement. Keep playing at the same level right to the last second.
Instrumental only, no vocals, no humming. Avoid: an intro or count-in, breakdowns or drop-outs, big drum fills, cymbal crashes, risers, saxophone or guitar solos, key or tempo changes, any ending or fade-out, and anything bright, electronic or dance-like.
